title: Short exact sequences in the heart are triangles
statement:
Let $(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ be a t-structure on a
triangulated category $\mathcal T$ in the sense of [def-weil-t-structure]
(not necessarily bounded), and let $\mathcal A=\mathcal
T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ be its heart, which is abelian by
[prop-weil-heart-abelian].

1. (*Truncations.*) For every $K\in\mathcal T$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$ the
   triangle $\tau^{\le n}K\to K\to\tau^{\ge n+1}K\to\tau^{\le n}K[1]$ with
   $\tau^{\le n}K\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $\tau^{\ge n+1}K\in\mathcal
   T^{\ge n+1}$ is unique up to unique isomorphism, and $\tau^{\le n}$,
   $\tau^{\ge n+1}$ are functors, right, respectively left, adjoint to the
   inclusions of $\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$. There is
   a canonical isomorphism $\tau^{\ge0}\tau^{\le0}\cong\tau^{\le0}\tau^{\ge0}$,
   and $H^0:=\tau^{\ge0}\tau^{\le0}:\mathcal T\to\mathcal A$; put
   $H^i(K):=H^0(K[i])$.
2. (*Extensions.*) $\mathcal T^{\le n}$, $\mathcal T^{\ge n}$ and
   $\mathcal A$ are closed under extensions: if $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ is
   distinguished and $X,Z$ lie in one of them, so does $Y$.
3. (*Kernels and cokernels.*) Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of $\mathcal A$
   and complete it to a distinguished triangle $X\xrightarrow fY\to S\to
   X[1]$. Then $S\in\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge-1}$,
   $$
   \ker f\cong H^{-1}(S)=(\tau^{\le-1}S)[-1],\qquad
   \operatorname{coker}f\cong H^0(S)=\tau^{\ge0}S,
   $$
   with the kernel map $(\tau^{\le-1}S)[-1]\to S[-1]\to X$ and the
   cokernel map $Y\to S\to\tau^{\ge0}S$.
4. (*Short exact sequences.*) A sequence $0\to X\xrightarrow fY
   \xrightarrow gZ\to0$ of $\mathcal A$ is short exact if and only if
   there is a morphism $\delta:Z\to X[1]$ such that $X\xrightarrow fY
   \xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow\delta X[1]$ is distinguished, and then
   $\delta$ is unique. In particular a distinguished triangle whose three
   terms lie in $\mathcal A$ is a short exact sequence of $\mathcal A$.
5. (*Cohomological functor.*) $H^0$ is cohomological: a distinguished
   triangle $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ gives a long exact sequence in
   $\mathcal A$
   $$
   \cdots\to H^{i}(X)\to H^{i}(Y)\to H^{i}(Z)\to H^{i+1}(X)\to\cdots .
   $$

(*Source: Beilinson--Bernstein--Deligne, Faisceaux pervers, 1.3.3--1.3.6
and 1.1.9--1.1.10; no Stacks Project entry states this form, for the
reasons recorded at [def-weil-t-structure].*)

proof.text: Shift the three axioms of [def-weil-t-structure] to level $n$. They give $\mathcal T^{\le n-1}\subseteq\mathcal T^{\le n}$, $\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}\subseteq\mathcal T^{\ge n}$, vanishing $\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q)=0$ for $P\le n<Q$, and a triangle $A\xrightarrow a K\xrightarrow b B\xrightarrow d A[1]$ with $A\le n$, $B\ge n+1$. In all following steps, exactness of covariant Hom means [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact], and exactness of contravariant Hom means [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact], applied also to signed rotations supplied by [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Thus each vanishing composite has the asserted factorization; neither lemma asserts uniqueness without an additional vanishing argument.

source.place: 1.3.1, 1.3.3 proof; compare Stacks Tags 0146 and 0149, derived.tex, lemma-composition-zero and lemma-representable-homological

proof.text: For $P\le n$, covariant Hom exactness and $\operatorname{Hom}(P,B[-1])=\operatorname{Hom}(P,B)=0$ show that composition with $a$ bijects $\operatorname{Hom}(P,A)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(P,K)$. Dually, for $Q\ge n+1$, $\operatorname{Hom}(A[1],Q)=\operatorname{Hom}(A,Q)=0$ show that precomposition with $b$ bijects $\operatorname{Hom}(B,Q)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(K,Q)$. For a map $K\to K'$, these bijections uniquely define maps $A\to A'$ and $B\to B'$. Uniqueness proves preservation of identities and composition, naturality of $a,b$, and the two adjunctions. Two choices are uniquely isomorphic under/over $K$: apply the bijections to the structure maps in both directions; the composites are identities by their uniqueness. TR3 extends the map on $A,K$ to a triangle morphism, and its component on $B$ must be the already constructed one by the second bijection. In particular it respects $d$. For two possible $d,d'$ on fixed $a,b$, TR3 gives $h:B\to B$ with $hb=b$ and $d'h=d$. Contravariant Hom exactness factors $h-1$ through $d$ via a map $A[1]\to B$, which is zero since $A[1]\le n-1$ and $B\ge n+1$. Thus $h=1$ and $d=d'$. This proves uniqueness of the entire truncation triangle fixing $K$. The Hom bijections respect addition, so the truncation functors are additive.

These bijections also give the orthogonal characterizations without a boundedness assumption. If $\operatorname{Hom}(P,K)=0$ for every $P\le n$, taking $P=A$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}(A,A)=0$, so $A=0$. Hom exactness for $0\to K\xrightarrow b B\to0$ makes composition with $b$ a bijection on every represented Hom set; evaluating at $B$ and $K$ supplies a two-sided inverse, so $K\simeq B\ge n+1$. Conversely this membership gives the stated vanishing by orthogonality. If instead $\operatorname{Hom}(K,Q)=0$ for every $Q\ge n+1$, the second bijection of step 2 with $Q=B$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}(B,B)=0$, hence $B=0$. Covariant Hom exactness for $A\xrightarrow a K\to0\to A[1]$ makes composition with $a$ bijective on $\operatorname{Hom}(W,-)$ for every $W$; taking $W=K,A$ gives an inverse for $a$. Thus $K\simeq A\le n$. Conversely $K\le n$ implies this Hom vanishing by orthogonality. In particular $\tau^{\le n}K=0$ iff $K\ge n+1$, and $\tau^{\ge n+1}K=0$ iff $K\le n$.

If $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ is distinguished and $X,Z\ge n+1$, covariant Hom exactness gives $\operatorname{Hom}(P,Y)=0$ for every $P\le n$, since its two neighbouring groups vanish. Step 3 implies $Y\ge n+1$. If $X,Z\le n$, then for each $Q\ge n+1$ the exact sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Z,Q)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Y,Q)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X,Q)$ has zero outer groups. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,Q)=0$ for all such $Q$, and step 3 gives $Y\le n$. Intersecting at level zero proves extension closure of the heart. This proves clause (2) before using it in clause (1).

For $K\le b$, rotate its truncation triangle at $a-1$ to $K\to\tau^{\ge a}K\to(\tau^{\le a-1}K)[1]\to$. If $a\le b$, both endpoints are $\le b$, hence $\tau^{\ge a}K\le b$ by step 4. Still assuming $a\le b$, for $K\ge a$, inverse rotation of the truncation triangle at $b$ gives endpoints $(\tau^{\ge b+1}K)[-1]\ge b+2\ge a$ and $K\ge a$, so $\tau^{\le b}K\ge a$. In particular both $\tau^{\ge0}\tau^{\le0}K$ and $\tau^{\le0}\tau^{\ge0}K$ lie in the heart. The universal properties also show $\tau^{\le a}\tau^{\le b}\simeq\tau^{\le a}$ for $a\le b$: both represent $\operatorname{Hom}(-,K)$ on $\mathcal T^{\le a}$. For $Q\ge b$, the left adjunction twice identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(\tau^{\ge b}\tau^{\ge a}K,Q)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(\tau^{\ge a}K,Q)=\operatorname{Hom}(K,Q)$, since $Q\ge b\ge a$. Thus $\tau^{\ge b}\tau^{\ge a}\simeq\tau^{\ge b}$ by the uniqueness of the representing object. These identifications are natural because they preserve the representing maps.

Apply TR4 to $\tau^{\le-1}K\to\tau^{\le0}K\to K$. The composite is the truncation map at $-1$, by the universal property in step 5. The three cones are $H=\tau^{\ge0}\tau^{\le0}K$, $\tau^{\ge1}K$, and $\tau^{\ge0}K$. The octahedron therefore gives a distinguished triangle $H\to\tau^{\ge0}K\to\tau^{\ge1}K\to H[1]$, with the comparison maps commuting with the structure maps from $\tau^{\le0}K$ and $K$. As $H\le0$ and $\tau^{\ge1}K\ge1$, step 2 identifies its first term with $\tau^{\le0}\tau^{\ge0}K$. The comparison is the unique map characterized by those commuting squares: first factor $\tau^{\le0}K\to\tau^{\ge0}K$ through $\tau^{\ge0}\tau^{\le0}K$ using the left adjunction, then factor to $\tau^{\le0}\tau^{\ge0}K$ using the right adjunction. These factorizations are natural, so the isomorphism is canonical and natural. Together with step 5 this defines the additive heart-valued functor $H^0$. Shifting the representing bijections proves $\tau^{\le a}(K[r])\simeq(\tau^{\le a+r}K)[r]$, and likewise for $\tau^{\ge a}$. In particular $H^{-1}(S)\simeq(\tau^{\ge-1}\tau^{\le-1}S)[-1]$. The nested-truncation identifications imply $H^0(\tau^{\le0}K)\simeq H^0K$ and $H^0(\tau^{\ge0}K)\simeq H^0K$, compatibly with the canonical truncation maps.

source.place: 1.3.5, octahedron (1.3.5.1) at a=b=0; 1.3.6 definition of H⁰

proof.text: Let $f:X\to Y$ be in the heart and choose a distinguished triangle $X\xrightarrow fY\to S\to X[1]$ using TR1. Its rotation exhibits $S$ as an extension of $X[1]$ by $Y$. Both lie in $\mathcal T^{\le0}\cap\mathcal T^{\ge-1}$, so step 4 puts $S$ there. Step 5 puts $\tau^{\le-1}S$ in degree $-1$ alone and $\tau^{\ge0}S$ in the heart. Consequently $K=(\tau^{\le-1}S)[-1]$ and $Q=\tau^{\ge0}S$ are heart objects. Step 6 identifies them with $H^{-1}(S)$ and $H^0(S)$ respectively.

For any heart object $T$, contravariant Hom exactness gives $\operatorname{Hom}(X[1],T)\to\operatorname{Hom}(S,T)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X,T)$. The first term vanishes, and the left adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,T)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(S,T)$. Thus $Y\to S\to Q$ is a cokernel of $f$, including uniqueness of factorization. In the inverse-rotated triangle, covariant Hom exactness gives $\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y[-1])\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,S[-1])\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,Y)$, with first group zero. The right adjunction and shift compatibility identify $\operatorname{Hom}(T,K)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(T,S[-1])$. Therefore the displayed map $K\to S[-1]\to X$ is a kernel of $f$. These are universal properties inside the full heart, not an appeal to a general Yoneda lemma. This proves clause (3).

Use the abelian structure of the heart from [prop-weil-heart-abelian]. If $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\to X[1]$ is distinguished with $X,Y,Z$ in the heart, steps 7–8 with $S=Z$ give $\ker f=0$ and say that $g$ is a cokernel of $f$. Thus $f$ is monic and the sequence is short exact. Conversely, for a short exact sequence choose the cone $S$ of $f$. Since $\ker f=0$, step 8 gives $\tau^{\le-1}S=0$. The truncation triangle then identifies $S$ with $\tau^{\ge0}S$, so $S$ is in the heart. Both $Y\to S$ and $g:Y\to Z$ are cokernels of $f$ in that abelian category. Their universal properties give inverse maps $S\simeq Z$ commuting with the maps from $Y$. Conjugate the cone triangle by this isomorphism using TR1 to obtain the required $\delta$. If $\delta,\delta'$ both work, TR3 with identities on $X,Y$ gives $h:Z\to Z$ with $hg=g$ and $\delta'h=\delta$. Contravariant Hom exactness factors $h-1$ through $\delta$ via $X[1]\to Z$, which vanishes since $X[1]\le-1$ and $Z\ge0$. Hence $h=1$ and $\delta'=\delta$. This proves clause (4).

For a distinguished triangle with all three terms $\ge0$, step 2 gives natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(T,H^0K)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(T,K)$ for heart objects $T$. Covariant Hom exactness, including $\operatorname{Hom}(T,Z[-1])=0$, says that the first map $H^0X\to H^0Y$ is a kernel of the second: maps killed by the second factor uniquely through the first. This is precisely $0\to H^0X\to H^0Y\to H^0Z$ exact. For a triangle with all terms $\le0$, use instead $\operatorname{Hom}(H^0K,T)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(K,T)$. Contravariant Hom exactness and $\operatorname{Hom}(X[1],T)=0$ show that $H^0Y\to H^0Z$ is a cokernel of $H^0X\to H^0Y$. In the abelian heart a cokernel is epic and its kernel is the image of the preceding map. This proves $H^0X\to H^0Y\to H^0Z\to0$ exact. Only the supplied abelian structure and these kernel/cokernel universal properties enter.

Suppose only $Z\ge0$. Apply TR4 to $\tau^{\le-1}X\to X\to Y$, choosing a cone $Y''$ of the composite. It gives triangles $\tau^{\le-1}X\to Y\to Y''\to$ and $\tau^{\ge0}X\to Y''\to Z\to$. Their squares state that $Y\to Y''\to Z$ is the original $g$ and that the square from $X\to Y$ to $\tau^{\ge0}X\to Y''$ commutes. Step 4 gives $Y''\ge0$, so the first triangle is the truncation triangle at $-1$ by step 2; hence $Y''\simeq\tau^{\ge0}Y$ compatibly with $Y\to Y''$. The second triangle has all terms $\ge0$, so step 10 applies. The natural $H^0$-isomorphisms of step 6 identify its first two terms and arrows with $H^0X\to H^0Y$. Thus $0\to H^0X\to H^0Y\to H^0Z$ is exact.

proof.text: Suppose only $X\le0$. Complete $Y\to Z\to\tau^{\ge1}Z$ to a triangle $Y'\to Y\to\tau^{\ge1}Z\to$ (TR1 and inverse rotation). Write $L=\tau^{\le0}Z$ and $R=\tau^{\ge1}Z$. For $Y\to Z\to R$, the cones of the first map, second map and composite are respectively $X[1]$, $L[1]$ and $Y'[1]$, using the rotations of the original triangle, the truncation triangle and the chosen triangle. TR4 gives $X[1]\xrightarrow\alpha Y'[1]\xrightarrow\beta L[1]\to X[2]$. Its commuting squares give $v[1]\alpha=f[1]$ and $l[1]\beta=g[1]v[1]$, where $v:Y'\to Y$ and $l:L\to Z$. Shifting by $[-1]$ gives the distinguished triangle with first two arrows $\alpha[-1]$ and $\beta[-1]$ and the negative shifted connecting map (this sign follows from three inverse rotations). Thus one obtains a triangle $X\to Y'\to\tau^{\le0}Z\to$ and squares with $X\to Y\to Z$: the square on first arrows commutes, and $Y'\to Y\to Z$ equals $Y'\to\tau^{\le0}Z\to Z$. Step 4 gives $Y'\le0$. Therefore $Y'\to Y\to\tau^{\ge1}Z$ is a truncation triangle at zero, so $Y'\simeq\tau^{\le0}Y$ compatibly with $Y'\to Y$. Apply the right-exact half of step 10 to $X\to Y'\to\tau^{\le0}Z$. By step 6 and the indicated commuting squares its image is $H^0X\to H^0Y\to H^0Z\to0$, with the original arrows. This establishes the other half of blueprint (5)(b), including the necessary map comparisons.

source.place: 1.3.6 proof, Cas 2; TR4′ is TR4 after signed inverse rotations

proof.text: For an arbitrary triangle $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$, apply TR4 to $\tau^{\le0}X\to X\to Y$. With $W$ the cone of the composite it supplies triangles $\tau^{\le0}X\to Y\to W\to$ and $\tau^{\ge1}X\to W\to Z\to$, and the equation $Y\to W\to Z=g$. Step 12 on the first triangle gives an exact sequence $H^0X\to H^0Y\to H^0W\to0$, using step 6 on its first map. Rotate the second triangle to $W\to Z\to(\tau^{\ge1}X)[1]\to$. Its third term is $\ge0$, so step 11 makes $H^0W\to H^0Z$ monic. Hence a map to $H^0Y$ is killed by $H^0g$ exactly when it is killed by $H^0Y\to H^0W$; the latter has kernel equal to the image of $H^0X\to H^0Y$. This proves exactness at $H^0Y$ for every distinguished triangle.

The additivity established in steps 2 and 6, and step 13 applied also to rotated triangles, show that $H^0$ is homological in the terminology of [def-sp-homological-functor] (the covariant cohomological convention of BBD). Apply [lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle] to this functor, with its abelian target given by [prop-weil-heart-abelian], and use the tautological shifted functors $H^i(K)=H^0(K[i])$. It gives exactly $\cdots\to H^iX\to H^iY\to H^iZ\to H^{i+1}X\to\cdots$, naturally in the triangle. The boundary is $H^0$ of the shifted third map, with the standard shift comparison; signed rotations change neighbouring maps by signs, which do not change their kernels or images. This proves clause (5).
